text:
maria-eng: heads up — monitoring alert: huge pending GPU pod backlog in eu-west-2 and a barrage of CA scale events :fire:

maria-eng: kubectl get pods -n inference | grep Pending | wc -l -> 462 pending pods

maria-eng: kubectl describe pod inference-xyz shows: 

maria-eng: ```Events:
  Normal  Scheduled  3s  default-scheduler  Successfully assigned ... to ip-10-0-xx-yy
  Warning FailedScheduling  3s  default-scheduler  0/40 nodes are available: 40 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```

autoscaler-bot: ASG/gpu-inference-eu-west-2 scaled from 8 -> 48 (requested) due to pending pods count 462

sam-sre: looking. Do we have an ongoing driver/daemonset rollout?

maria-eng: yes — raj kicked an image update for nvidia-device-plugin yesterday at ~0300 UTC. rollout went out across nodepools at 02:45 but it looks like a subset of nodes never became Ready for GPU resources

raj-infra: on it. checking node registration: `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu`

raj-infra: seeing ~12 nodes with KubeletReady=False and they all show kubelet logs: `failed to register device plugin: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection refused`

kai-ml: that explains CA: it thinks pods need GPUs so it spins up instances, but new instances fail to advertise GPUs -> they remain NotReady -> CA keeps scaling up -> feedback loop

maria-eng: exact symptom: scale-up, nodes not registering GPUs, cluster-autoscaler keeps requesting more, pods stay pending. Costly.

sam-sre: immediate mitigations: 1) pause CA scaling, 2) cordon/taint bad nodes, 3) revert device-plugin rollout or roll forward with fix, 4) reduce ASG max.

raj-infra: implemented 1 + 4: decreased ASG max to 20 (was 100) for gpu-inference-eu-west-2 and temporarily set cluster-autoscaler min/max to 8/20 via patch.

ops-bot: command run: `aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-inference-eu-west-2 --max-size 20`

maria-eng: good. I also cordoned the unhealthy nodes: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-24-11` x12 and applied taint `gpu-rollout-failed=true:NoSchedule` to prevent CA from considering them for scheduling until we fix the device plugin.

autoscaler-bot: cluster-autoscaler paused via ConfigMap: `scaleDownEnabled: false` and autoscaler status: paused-by-incident-maria-eng

raj-infra: dug into the daemonset logs — the new image is crashing on nodes that have older kernel module version. Crash trace: `fatal: nvidia-smi not found, plugin exiting` on nodes with kernel 5.10. Older nodes had driver mismatch.

kai-ml: we saw in rollout notes that kernel/driver matrix wasn't fully validated. We need a safer rollout: node selector or progressive canary.

maria-eng: short-term plan: revert to previous known-good device-plugin image across all nodepools (rollback), then restart kubelet on affected nodes, then re-enable CA with conservative thresholds.

raj-infra: rolling back daemonset now: `kubectl rollout undo ds/nvidia-device-plugin -n kube-system --to-revision=3`

raj-infra: restarting kubelet via SSM for the 12 affected nodes and rebooting 2 that failed to recover.

sam-sre: also setting CA flags to `--expendable-pods-priority-cutoff=200` and `--max-node-provision-time=10m` to avoid endless upscales while nodes remain NotReady.

maria-eng: checked costs: billing alarm already triggered. we avoided huge surge by cutting ASG max. need a postmortem to change rollout process.

kai-ml: quick test: after rollback and kubelet restarts, `kubectl get nodes | grep Ready | grep gpu | wc -l` -> 36 Ready GPUs, pending pods dropping: 462 -> 40

maria-eng: nice. now gradual re-enable CA: set max 40, enable scaleDown, watch for 30m

autoscaler-bot: cluster-autoscaler resumed; now observing scale-down activity.

ops-bot: incident label applied: `severity:high`, `issue:gpu-driver-rollout`

sam-sre: follow-ups for postmortem: 
- add kernel-driver compatibility matrix to the rollout checklist
- require canary on a single nodepool with metric gating (nvidia-smi presence)
- add a pre-rollout job that runs `nvidia-smi` on a sample of nodes and fails the rollout if missing
- CA tuning: add cooldown threshold for GPU failure cases

maria-eng: agreed. I'll open a postmortem PR and assign owners.

raj-infra: also will add automation to revert daemonset automatically if more than X nodes report `device-plugin exiting` within 10m.

kai-ml: thanks all. I'll close the alert once pending < 10 and no further scale events for 30m.

maria-eng: update: at 1708502000 pending pods 6, autoscaler steady. marking incident as mitigated but will keep watch for 2 hours. :thumbsup:
